topic: Data Preprocessing: Handling Outliers, Missing Values, and Skewed Data

questions.scenario: A high-frequency FinTech fraud detection engine processes a continuous stream of credit card transactions featuring 65 continuous metrics per event. The system has a strict inference Service Level Agreement (SLA) of less than 15 milliseconds per transaction. Univariate Z-score and IQR-based filtering fail to capture sophisticated multi-attribute fraud patterns. Implementing Mahalanobis Distance resulted in runtime bottlenecks due to covariance matrix inversion overhead and rank deficiency from multicollinearity. Meanwhile, Local Outlier Factor (LOF) violated SLA limits due to O(N^2) pairwise distance computations against the dynamic reference buffer.
questions.question: Which outlier detection algorithm best satisfies the sub-15ms throughput constraint while effectively isolating multivariate anomalies without assuming parametric normality?
options: A) Minimum Covariance Determinant (MCD) estimator combined with robust Mahalanobis distance calculation
B) Isolation Forest utilizing fixed subsample sizes (psi = 256) per isolation tree
C) Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) using a Ball-Tree index
D) Elliptic Envelope fitted via online Stochastic Gradient Descent
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Isolation Forest utilizing fixed subsample sizes (psi = 256) per isolation tree
questions.explanation: Isolation Forest explicitly isolates anomalies instead of profiling normal data points. Because anomalies require fewer random recursive partitions along feature axes, they exhibit noticeably shorter path lengths in isolation trees. By capping the subsampling size to psi = 256, the algorithm achieves an inference time complexity of O(t * log(psi)), where t is the number of trees. This decouples inference latency from dataset size N, easily satisfying the 15ms latency constraint, while successfully capturing multivariate anomalies without assuming Gaussian distribution or inverting high-dimensional covariance matrices.

questions.scenario: A healthcare analytics platform predicts septic shock onset in Intensive Care Units (ICU) across 40 continuous biomarkers. A key clinical biomarker, Serum Lactate, contains 38% missing values. Statistical diagnostics determine that the data mechanism is Missing Not At Random (MNAR); physicians systematically order lactate assays only when patients manifest overt signs of physiological distress. The engineering team observes that applying standard Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) with Predictive Mean Matching artificially shifts the hazard ratio distribution and introduces severe selection bias into the downstream generalized linear model.
questions.question: What is the most statistically sound strategy to process this feature without violating clinical assumptions and biasing the linear model coefficients?
options: A) Apply K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) imputation weighted by Euclidean distance over non-missing physiological vitals
B) Perform Complete Case Analysis (listwise deletion) to ensure zero synthetic data corruption
C) Generate an explicit binary missingness indicator column and impute missing values with a domain-neutral baseline or conditional median
D) Impute missing values using Mean substitution combined with standard Min-Max scaling
questions.correct_answer_text: C) Generate an explicit binary missingness indicator column and impute missing values with a domain-neutral baseline or conditional median
questions.explanation: Standard imputation algorithms (such as MICE, Mean, and KNN) operate under the assumption of Missing Completely At Random (MCAR) or Missing At Random (MAR). When data is Missing Not At Random (MNAR), the probability of missingness is causally linked to unobserved or clinical intent variables (i.e., missingness itself carries predictive information regarding the patient's low acuity). Under the Missing Indicator Method (Pattern-Mixture Modeling framework), appending a binary indicator flag (1 if missing, 0 otherwise) alongside an imputed conditional value preserves the informative missingness pattern, enabling downstream linear models to learn the distinct risks associated with test non-ordering.

questions.scenario: An enterprise supply chain platform is designing a demand forecasting pipeline for replacement aircraft components. The target feature, Daily Part Demand, exhibits extreme positive skewness (skewness coefficient = 5.8) and contains exact zero values on 32% of operational days (intermittent demand). The downstream architecture relies on L1/L2 regularized linear regression (ElasticNet), which strictly requires homoscedasticity and approximately normally distributed error terms. The team attempts a Box-Cox power transform, which immediately raises an arithmetic domain error.
questions.question: Which transformation strategy mathematically resolves the domain failure while optimizing parameter estimation to stabilize error variance and normalize the feature distribution?
options: A) Apply the Yeo-Johnson power transformation optimized via profile Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)
B) Apply Box-Cox after adding an arbitrarily large empirical constant offset (c = 1000) to all observations
C) Apply standard Log1p transformation (log(x + 1)) without parameter estimation
D) Apply Quantile Transformation mapped to a Uniform Distribution with 10,000 empirical quantiles
questions.correct_answer_text: A) Apply the Yeo-Johnson power transformation optimized via profile Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)
questions.explanation: The Box-Cox transform is mathematically restricted to strictly positive real values (y > 0), causing domain runtime exceptions when zero values exist. While an ad-hoc shift like log1p (log(x + 1)) accommodates non-negative values, it enforces a rigid transformation parameter (equivalent to lambda = 0) that cannot guarantee variance stabilization or optimal residual normality across diverse tail behaviors. The Yeo-Johnson power transformation extends Box-Cox methodology to allow zero and negative values through a continuous piecewise function, using profile Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) to estimate an optimal power parameter lambda that stabilizes variance and induces normality.
